statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, r equals the minimized maximum pair sum of nums. Precisely, a perfect pairing of nums is a partition of the index set {0, ..., len(nums)-1} into len(nums)/2 unordered pairs {i,j} of distinct indices; the maximum pair sum of such a pairing is the largest value nums[i]+nums[j] over its pairs; and r is the least integer M for which there exists a perfect pairing of nums all of whose pair sums are <= M.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, min_pair_sum nums returns a result (it does not fail, overflow, or panic).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, r >= L + S, where L is the largest element of nums and S is the smallest element of nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let b0 >= b1 >= ... >= b_{len(nums)-1} be a nonincreasing rearrangement of nums, with duplicates counted separately. Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, r <= b0 + b1.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, r >= ceil(T / (len(nums)/2)), where T = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] and ceil(x) is the least integer greater than or equal to x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, there exists a perfect pairing P of nums, where a perfect pairing is a partition of {0, ..., len(nums)-1} into len(nums)/2 unordered pairs of distinct indices, such that every pair {i,j} in P satisfies nums[i]+nums[j] <= r, and at least one pair {i,j} in P satisfies nums[i]+nums[j] = r.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r and min_pair_sum nums' returns a result r', we have r' = r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers; both satisfy the problem constraints (even length between 2 and 100000 and all entries between 1 and 100000); len(nums') = len(nums); and there is a bijection sigma on {0, ..., len(nums)-1} such that nums'[i] = nums[sigma(i)] for every i.

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r and min_pair_sum nums' returns a result r', we have r' = r + 2*c.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers; both satisfy the problem constraints (even length between 2 and 100000 and all entries between 1 and 100000); len(nums') = len(nums); and there is an integer c such that nums'[i] = nums[i] + c for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r and min_pair_sum nums' returns a result r', we have r' = k*r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers; both satisfy the problem constraints (even length between 2 and 100000 and all entries between 1 and 100000); len(nums') = len(nums); and there is a positive integer k such that nums'[i] = k*nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r and min_pair_sum nums' returns a result r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers; both satisfy the problem constraints (even length between 2 and 100000 and all entries between 1 and 100000); len(nums') = len(nums); and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums'[i] >= nums[i].

statement: Let a0 <= a1 <= ... <= a_{len(nums)-1} be a nondecreasing rearrangement of nums, with duplicates counted separately. Whenever min_pair_sum nums returns a result r, r = max_{0 <= i < len(nums)/2} (a_i + a_{len(nums)-1-i}).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; len(nums) is even; 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
